Durability

/dur-uh-BIL-ih-tee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Durability means the ability to withstand wear, damage, or decay over a long time.

Elena chose her hiking boots for their durability; after five years of rocky trails, the stitching has not frayed and the soles are still solid.

Worked Example

The cast-iron skillet in Ruth's kitchen belonged to her great-grandmother. A century of nearly daily cooking has left it as sturdy as ever, living proof of its durability.

The skillet has faced one hundred years of heat, scraping, and use, and it still works perfectly. Withstanding that much wear over that much time without failing is exactly what durability means.

How Durability Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

toughness

toughness: strength against damage

longevity

longevity: long life or lasting existence

ruggedness

ruggedness: sturdy build for rough conditions

Antonyms

fragility

fragility: quality of breaking easily

flimsiness

flimsiness: weak, thin construction

How Strong Is It? — sturdiness → durability → indestructibility

sturdiness vs. durability

sturdiness vs. durability: Sturdiness means something is solidly built right now, while durability means it will keep holding up through years of wear and use.

indestructibility vs. durability

indestructibility vs. durability: Durability means something withstands long use and damage, while indestructibility claims it can never be destroyed at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — dur

Root — dur: hard, to last (Latin durare, to last, from durus, hard)

Suffix — -abil

Suffix — -abil: able to, capable of

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state or quality

Put it together

Put it together: Read the pieces in order and the word defines itself: the quality of being able to last. Something with durability is literally hard enough to keep lasting.

Use the root in a new word: endure

Use the root in a new word: endure: The stone lighthouse has endured two hundred years of pounding waves.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / consumer and engineering

Shows up constantly in product reviews and materials science, as in built for durability or tested for durability. Do not confuse it with duration, which is simply how long something goes on, not how well it holds up.
